# Growthbook <> Truemeds - Intro
Date: 2026-10-13 | Duration: 36.75m

## Summary
True Meds is seeking to increase experimentation speed because its current platform limits the team to 24 concurrent experiments, requires 1.5 to 2 months per experiment due to low traffic, and lacks Cupid, sequential testing, and long-term holdout capabilities. Growthbook said it supports unlimited experiments, Cupid, sequential testing, multi-armed bandits, power analysis, independent experiment layers, and unified metrics. True Meds is approximately 70% migrated to Snowflake and is comparing Growthbook’s managed event-based model with its warehouse-native experiment-based model. Cost, compute, USD-to-INR currency risk, implementation ease, and execution speed are key decision factors. The team is also renegotiating Mixpanel costs and assessing whether Growthbook could consolidate dashboards. Growthbook proposed a technical deep dive, product demo, and possible proof of concept, with follow-up sessions planned during Indian business hours.

## Keywords
Experimentation, Snowflake, Warehouse-native, Growthbook, Pricing, Analytics integration

## Action Items

**Dan Wathne**
Send follow-up email with proposed agenda and availability for Thursday/Friday sessions to conduct demo and technical integration with Truemeds team (34:00)
Provide ballpark pricing estimates based on expected experiment ramp-up and events tracked for both managed and warehouse-native options (23:15)

**Pranav Chavan**
Coordinate with analytics and technical leads (Arvind and Yash) to join next technical integration and demo session with Growthbook (31:50)
Share event volume, metrics tracked, and provide further info needed for accurate pricing and integration feasibility (23:50)

**Truemeds Analytics & Technical Leads**
Prepare for technical deep dive on Snowflake data warehousing setup, event pipelines, and integration requirements with Growthbook (18:40)

**All Participants**
Prepare questions and requirements especially around feature setup, experiment run management, analytics overlap with Mixpanel, and pricing concerns for next meeting (31:00)
